newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Storm swamps Bangladesh coast, kills at least four.
newsitem.headline: Storm swamps Bangladesh coast, kills at least four.

text.p: Four children were killed and at least 100 people were injured when a storm in the Bay of Bengal ravaged Bangladesh's coast early on Tuesday, officials said.
They said at least 20 people were missing after three boats sank in a river in Bhola district, where a storm surge up to nine feet (three metres) high swamped the coast.
"Thousands of cattle have been washed away," one official in Chittagong said.
"Some 400 houses have been destroyed, leaving thousands of people homeless," said a police officer in Barisal district.
At least 100 people were injured, officials with the Cyclone Preparedness Programme said.
More than 10,000 people remained huddled in storm shelters in Bhola, officials there said.
Heavy rain triggered by the storm swept the coast and inland districts, including the capital, Dhaka. Many streets in Dhaka were flooded, witnesses said.
The center of the storm passed over the Sundarban forests, but officials in the nearby town of Khulna said they had no immediate reports of casualties or major damage.
"Winds up to 65 kph (40 mph) hit the coast and offshore islands around 3 a.m. before roaring towards India's West Bengal coast," one official in southern Khulna district said.
"Sea waves triggered by the storm briefly inundated vast areas, including homes and crop fields," he told reporters.
Thousands of fishing boats rushed to shore after storm Warnings were issued over the radio.
